instantiated_cells.justification: Principals must file expense statements on or before July 31 and January 31 (semiannual), not annually.
The statute sets filing deadlines of July 31 and January 31, not monthly reports.
The law specifies a semiannual schedule (July 31 and January 31) and does not provide another periodic filing frequency option for principals' expense statements.
Expense statements are due twice per year, not quarterly.
Registered principals must file expense statements on or before July 31 and January 31 for each preceding 6-month reporting period, i.e., semiannually.
The statute requires filing by fixed dates (July 31 and January 31) rather than three times per year linked to the legislative calendar.
The principal registration statement must describe the principal's business activity or nature and purposes, requiring disclosure of the nature of the business/organization.
The expense statement's aggregate total must include compensation to lobbyists for lobbying, in cash or in-kind.
The required contents of the principal's expense statement include expenditures, time records, and certain reimbursements, but do not require reporting each lobbying contact/communication.
Principals must report each legislative proposal, budget bill subject, proposed administrative rule number, or (if none) each topic of lobbying communication with reasonable specificity.
Expense statements must list the officials/candidates reimbursed under §13.625(7) and the date and amount reimbursed, covering expense categories such as travel/living expenses authorized by §19.56.
Principals must report aggregate overhead/indirect costs such as office space, utilities, supplies, and compensation of employees used in preparing for lobbying communications.
If payments to any lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period, the principal must list the lobbyist's name and address, which includes contracted lobbyists.
The expense statement requires listing each lobbyist (by name and address) whose compensation/reimbursement from the principal exceeds $200 in the reporting period.
Neither the registration statement nor the expense statement requires disclosure of the principal’s major financial contributors.
A principal exceeding the threshold must file a registration statement specifying the principal's name and business address.

Principals must report each legislative proposal and proposed administrative rule number (i.e., specific numbered items) in connection with which they have made or intend to make a lobbying communication.
The expense statement must report the aggregate total amount of lobbying expenditures made and obligations incurred for lobbying by the principal and all lobbyists for the principal.
The expense statement must include lobbyist compensation in the aggregate total and, if payments to a lobbyist exceed $200, list that lobbyist and the total amount paid/incurred for that lobbyist.
The statute generally requires aggregated totals (e.g., aggregate total lobbying expenditures and obligations), not full itemization of each expenditure.
Associations must report the chief executive officer and approximate number of members, but the statute does not require listing the names of all sponsors or members.
Principals' expense statements must list by name and address each lobbyist for whom lobbying expenditures/obligations exceed $200 during the reporting period.
